title: Framing Challenging Assignments Positively
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This Field Note dissects how leaders frame stretch assignments by laying out six sample scripts ranging from confident encouragement to pessimistic discouragement, showing how subtly different wording sends very different messages about a leader's confidence. It argues that team members tackling unfamiliar territory need support and confidence up front, and that concerns about difficulty should be saved for later once a plan of action exists. A key finding is that leaders often believe they're being encouraging when, on paper, their actual words read as pessimistic -- meaning framing needs to be rehearsed and reviewed rather than left to the moment.
points: Six sample scripts illustrate the spectrum from confident encouragement to pessimistic discouragement when assigning stretch work.
Team members facing challenging assignments need confidence and support up front, not caveats about failure.
Leaders often misjudge their own tone, believing they sound encouraging when their words read as pessimistic.
Concerns about difficulty are best saved for later, once the team member has proposed a plan of action.
Rehearsing and reviewing how framing will land is recommended rather than delivering it off the cuff.
quotes: How leaders frame the challenge varies along a continuum from positive to negative, from optimistic to pessimistic, and from encouraging to forewarning.
I have the utmost confidence in you to tackle this assignment. You’ll do great and learn a lot.
They know confidence drives high performance and they go out of their way to provide it.
It is surprising how often leaders think they have been optimistic and encouraging when they have actually delivered a pessimistic and discouraging message.
Framing situations in the positive is a crucially important leadership skill. Practice makes perfect.
